takeaways: Senior housing hits 89.9% occupancy — its 20th straight quarterly gain — with $33.3B in trailing-12-month investment sales, up 83%. The demand-supply setup keeps improving for operators.
FIFA scrapped its $20B World Cup commercial-rights sale just 72 hours after the plan leaked — JPMorgan's pitch collapsed under global backlash.
Trump called off a fresh strike on Iran, saying 'the perimeters of a deal' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz are agreed — potential relief for freight costs and rate-sensitive CRE markets.

items.headline: Senior housing occupancy hits 89.9%, 20th consecutive quarterly gain
items.summary: Occupied units rose nearly 3,700 in Q2 to 639,650, and NIC expects occupancy to top 90% before year-end. With fewer than 16,000 units under construction, the supply-demand imbalance keeps strengthening pricing power for operators like Lloyd Jones.

items.headline: Senior housing investment sales surge 83% to $33.3B
items.summary: Trailing-12-month investment sales through May reached $33.3 billion, up 83% year-over-year. Ventas alone has deployed nearly $5.7 billion into U.S. senior housing acquisitions since late 2024, including $1.7 billion this year — institutional capital is back in force.

items.headline: FIFA scraps $20B World Cup commercial-rights sale after global revolt
items.summary: Barely 72 hours after a leaked plan to sell part of the World Cup's commercial rights sparked outrage, FIFA President Gianni Infantino abandoned the proposal. JPMorgan had pitched a $20 billion valuation on the deal before the stunning reversal. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Trump calls off new Iran attack, citing agreed deal framework
items.summary: President Trump called off a planned strike after Iranian drone attacks on Kuwait widened the conflict, saying 'the perimeters of a deal' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end Tehran's nuclear threat are agreed. De-escalation would ease the commodity and freight-cost pressures that have been pushing up prices economy-wide. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: HOA foreclosures hit 6,376 filings, up nearly 40% in two years
items.summary: HOA-related foreclosure filings reached 6,376 U.S. properties in Q1, up nearly 40% from two years earlier, as rising costs squeeze homeowners associations into taking a harder line on delinquent dues. A signal of household stress worth watching across residential real estate. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Warsh floats fewer Fed meetings in substantial policy shift
items.summary: Kevin Warsh has floated reducing the number of times the Federal Reserve meets to set interest rates — a substantial operational shift for the central bank. Fewer scheduled decisions could mean longer stretches of rate certainty, with implications for CRE debt pricing. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: How OpenAI lost its AI crown to Anthropic — and its fight back
items.summary: OpenAI fell behind Anthropic after betting on consumer chatbots and side projects while its rival seized the lead in AI coding. Its newest hire, Fields-level mathematician Jacob Tsimerman, joined believing AI safety is the most important problem he can solve. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Lone Star refinances senior housing portfolio with $235M note
items.summary: Lone Star Funds closed a $235 million refinancing across its senior housing portfolio, the latest sign that debt markets have reopened for the sector. Lenders re-engaging at scale supports valuations and exit optionality for operators and owners.

items.headline: Dealbook: Brookdale buys Houston community; Berkadia closes Fannie Mae loan
items.summary: Brookdale acquired the Brookdale Galleria community in Houston for $23.4 million, and Berkadia secured Fannie Mae financing for Vitality Living Franklin, a 126-unit AL/memory care community in Tennessee, on behalf of Clarion Partners. Deal flow remains competitive and selective.

items.headline: Mamdani's luxury second-home tax draws backlash from NY homeowners
items.summary: New York's new tax on luxury second homes is drawing complaints from homeowners who say the city wrongly flagged their primary residences as pieds-a-terre. The messy rollout comes as populist housing policies gain traction in key primaries nationwide. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Ellison takes $81B Warner deal to trial over California lawsuit
items.summary: After clearing regulators worldwide, David Ellison is taking his $81 billion Warner deal to trial to overcome a California lawsuit threatening the Paramount merger — one of the largest M&A fights in media history. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: CBRE: cap rates to compress 5-15 bps as banks re-enter CRE lending
items.summary: CBRE's 2026 outlook sees cap rates falling 5-15 basis points this year, with compression concentrated in higher-quality assets and ample dry powder keeping debt markets liquid. Traditional banks are lending again alongside private credit, setting up a robust year for originations.

items.headline: Silicon Valley races to build American alternative to cheap Chinese AI
items.summary: A new crop of startups is building open-weight AI models to compete with cheaper Chinese rivals like DeepSeek and Qwen, but many investors are reluctant to fund them — the race to challenge China is becoming as much a funding battle as a technology one. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Wachtell defections to Gibson Dunn shatter Big Law's old order
items.summary: Six partners left Wachtell for Gibson Dunn, shocking a legal world where poaching among white-shoe firms was unheard of and pay tracked seniority. Elite firms are losing rainmakers to bigger rivals offering NBA-star-level pay packages — a case study in talent-retention economics. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Mastercard's new CFO takes over today in leadership shakeup
items.summary: Ling Hai, President of APAC, Europe, Middle East and Africa, becomes Mastercard's CFO effective August 3, succeeding Sachin Mehra as part of broader leadership updates to advance strategy and support growth.

items.headline: Helicopter parents now co-pilot their adult children's careers
items.summary: Parents are increasingly managing adult children's careers — negotiating on their behalf and even lurking offscreen during Zoom meetings. What started as ride-alongs to job interviews has escalated into full-scale career co-piloting, a challenge for managers hiring Gen Z. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: JPMorgan: 71% of business leaders confident despite tougher economy
items.summary: JPMorgan's 2026 Business Leaders Outlook finds 71% of leaders confident in their own company's performance. New products/services top the strategy list (58%, up from 53%), with strategic partnerships rising to 49%.

items.headline: PwC: AI moves from experiment to efficiency driver in real estate
items.summary: PwC and ULI's Emerging Trends research finds AI shifting from pilot projects to practical operations across real estate — streamlining underwriting, leasing, and building management. The gap between adopters and holdouts keeps widening.

items.headline: National Wellness Month kicks off with focus on decision reduction
items.summary: August is National Wellness Month, and 2026's theme centers on simplicity: using routines, defaults, and systems to cut unnecessary decisions, reduce stress, and free up energy. A timely angle for resident-experience and staff-wellbeing programming.

items.headline: 89% of employees say wellbeing directly drives work performance
items.summary: Wellhub's 2026 State of Work-Life-Wellness report finds 89% of employees perform better when they prioritize wellbeing, positioning wellness investment as one of the highest-ROI talent strategies — relevant for senior living operators battling frontline turnover.
